sections.text:
1 Duas formas epistolae Petosiridis ad Nechepsonem, quae in multis codicibus
traditur, edidit Riess (Philologus, Supplband VI, p. 384 s.) Tertiam praebet codex
Mutinensis, cuius finis aliis est plenior. Ideo eam hic edere visum est. Computandi
methodus quae hic a Petosiride exponitur, traditur etiam in cod. Flor. 12, f. 23 (ubi
pro Ὑφίλα legendum esse ὕφειλαι monuit Kroll) et in cod. Neap. 19, f. 309
(cf. supra, p. 56). — De re, cf. Bouché-Leclercq, Astrol. grecque, p. 538 ss.
sections.en: 1 Two forms of the letter of Petosiris to Nechepso, which is transmitted in many codices, Riess edited (Philologus, Supplband VI, p. 384 f.). A third is offered by the Mutinensis codex, whose end is fuller than the others. Therefore it seemed good to edit it here. The method of computing which is expounded here by Petosiris, is transmitted also in cod. Flor. 12, f. 23 (where for Ὑφίλα it should be read ὕφειλαι Kroll advised) and in cod. Neap. 19, f. 309 (cf. above, p. 56). — On the matter, cf. Bouché-Leclercq, Astrol. grecque, p. 538 ff.

summary.headline: Petosiris’s Letter to Nechepso
summary.text: Letter of Petosiris the philosopher to King Nechepso presenting a numerical astrological method for judging illness, survival or death, gladiatorial victories, honor, and flight, with examples involving Achilles and Hector.
